s: Who is the President of COP31, which opened at Antalya on 9 November 2026?
x: Türkiye's Environment Minister Murat Kurum is COP31 President; Australia's Chris Bowen leads the negotiations.

s:
Consider the following statements about COP31:
1. It opened on 9 November 2026 at Antalya, Türkiye.
2. Australia leads the negotiations while Türkiye hosts and presides.
3. It is the first COP hosted by Türkiye.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: COP31 opened 9 Nov 2026 in Antalya, hosted by Türkiye for the first time, with Australia leading negotiations.

s: India's opening statement at UNFCCC COP31 (10 November 2026) was delivered by
x: MoEFCC Secretary Narendra Bhooshan delivered it; Minister Bhupender Yadav was to join in the second week.

s: Which of the following was NOT a position India stressed in its COP31 opening statement?
o: UNFCCC and Paris Agreement as the most inclusive platforms
Public finance from developed countries as central
x: India stressed equity, CBDR-RC, multilateralism and developed-country public finance; it has not joined the Global Methane Pledge.

s: The '35-by-35' Global Electrification Pledge promoted by the COP31 Presidency aims to
o: Raise electricity's share of global final energy consumption to 35% by 2035
Install 35 GW of offshore wind in each G20 country by 2035
x: It seeks to raise electricity's share of final energy from about 20–23% to 35% by 2035; it is voluntary.

s:
Consider the following about the 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge:
1. It was introduced by the Turkish COP31 Presidency at the Bonn Climate Conference in June 2026.
2. It is a legally binding target under the Paris Agreement.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: It was introduced at Bonn in June 2026 and is voluntary and non-binding.

s: India ratified the UNFCCC on
x: India signed at Rio in 1992 and ratified on 1 November 1993; the Convention entered into force on 21 March 1994.

s: According to the WMO State of the Climate 2026 report released at COP31, the global mean temperature for January–September 2026 was about how much above the 1850–1900 average?
x: WMO put Jan–Sep 2026 at 1.47°C above pre-industrial; 2026 is likely among the four warmest years.

s:
With reference to the WMO State of the Climate 2026, consider:
1. Atmospheric CO2 reached about 426.8 ppm in 2025, around 53% above 1750 levels.
2. Methane concentration in 2025 was about 1,948 ppb.
3. Oceans absorb about 50% of the excess heat in the Earth system.
Which of the above are correct?
x: CO2 426.8 ppm (+53%) and methane 1,948 ppb are correct; oceans absorb about 90%, not 50%, of excess heat.

s: As per the Global Carbon Budget 2026 (Global Carbon Project), global fossil CO2 emissions in 2026 are projected to be about
x: Fossil CO2 is projected at 38.2 Gt, a 0.4% fall; 43.3 Gt is the total including land-use change.

s: As per the Global Carbon Budget 2026, which country/bloc is projected to INCREASE its fossil CO2 emissions in 2026?
The Global Carbon Budget 2026 estimates the remaining carbon budget for limiting warming to 1.5°C at about
x: About 150 Gt CO2 remains – less than four years of current emissions.

s:
Consider the following about the 2026 Antarctic ozone hole:
1. It was the 7th largest on record.
2. It forms in the troposphere over Antarctica.
3. Polar stratospheric clouds provide surfaces for ozone-destroying reactions.
Which of the above are correct?
x: The 2026 hole was the 7th largest; it forms in the stratosphere, where polar stratospheric clouds inside the cold polar vortex drive ozone loss.

s: The study estimating that human-induced climate change raised the economic damage of Cyclone Arnab by about 33% was carried out by
x: Imperial College London's Grantham Institute used its IRIS storm model.

s: Cyclone Arnab (October 2026) actually crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near
x: It crossed on 28 Oct 2026 about 20 km ENE of Narsapur and 40 km SW of Yanam.

s:
Consider the following about Cyclone Murasu (November 2026):
1. It formed over the Southwest Bay of Bengal on 1 November 2026.
2. It was forecast to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur.
3. The name was proposed by Bangladesh.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Murasu formed on 1 Nov and was forecast between Nellore and Narsapur; the name is India's (Arnab was Bangladesh's).

s: Tropical cyclones do not generally form very close to the equator mainly because
o: The Coriolis force is too weak there
Sea surface temperature is below 27°C there
Wind shear is extremely high there
There is no latent heat release
x: A weak Coriolis force near the equator cannot initiate rotation.

s: Which district reported the largest number of drought-affected farmers in Rayalaseema during Kharif 2026?
x: Kurnool: about 1.85 lakh farmers and 1.68 lakh ha affected.

s: Meteorological drought is said to occur when rainfall is
x: Meteorological drought: rainfall 25% or more below normal.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The International Day for Biosphere Reserves is observed on 3 November.
2. India has 18 notified Biosphere Reserves, of which 13 are in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Both correct: UNESCO proclaimed the day in 2021 (first observed 2022); India has 18 BRs, 13 in the WNBR.

s: Gegeneophis chandgadi, discovered in Kolhapur district of Maharashtra in 2026, is a new species of
x: It is a caecilian, family Grandisoniidae, found at Buzawade village, Chandgad taluka.

s: How many caecilian species has India documented (as per the 2026 description of Gegeneophis chandgadi)?
x: India has 458 amphibian species including 41 caecilians; 12 are Gegeneophis.

s: Which of the following is NOT a cheetah habitat in Madhya Pradesh under India's cheetah reintroduction?
x: MP's sites are Kuno, Gandhi Sagar WLS and Veerangana Durgavati TR; Mukundra Hills is in Rajasthan.

s: Match the IUCN status: the African cheetah and the Asiatic cheetah are respectively
o: Vulnerable and Extinct in the Wild
x: African cheetah: Vulnerable; Asiatic cheetah (Iran): Critically Endangered.

s: Punyakshetram village in East Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh, is a traditional nesting site of
x: Asian Openbill Storks nest at Punyakshetram, Rajanagaram mandal.

s:
Consider the following about the Asian Openbill Stork:
1. It feeds mainly on freshwater snails.
2. It is listed as Endangered by IUCN.
3. It is in Schedule II of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Which of the above are correct?
x: It eats snails and is in Schedule II, but its IUCN status is Least Concern.

s: The Bay of Bengal Ocean Research Network (BOB-NOR), launched in November 2026, does NOT include which of these countries as a founding participant?
x: BOB-NOR was launched by India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and the Maldives at ICAR-CMFRI.

s: The BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week (1–7 November 2026) observed in Andhra Pradesh was organised around the themes of
x: Its daily activities followed the seven themes of Mission LiFE, under India's 2026 BRICS Presidency.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the green firecracker types developed by CSIR-NEERI?
x: The three are SWAS, STAR and SAFAL; SAMEER is the CPCB air-quality app.

s: What is India's rank in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2027 released at COP31?
x: India is 28th (60.85, Medium), down from 23rd in CCPI 2026 and 10th in CCPI 2025.

s: The Climate Change Performance Index is published by
x: CCPI is by Germanwatch and the NewClimate Institute (with Climate Action Network).

s:
Consider the following about CCPI 2027:
1. The first three ranks were left vacant.
2. Denmark was the best-performing country.
3. The UK was the only G20 member rated 'High'.
Which of the above are correct?
x: All correct: ranks 1–3 vacant, Denmark 4th (best), UK 7th the only G20 'High'.

s: Which country was ranked LAST in the CCPI 2027?
x: Iran 68th (last), USA 67th, Russia 66th, Saudi Arabia 65th.

s: In the Allianz Green Transition Tracker 2026 (5 Nov 2026), India was ranked
x: India rose five places to 45th of 65 economies; Luxembourg topped.

s:
As per the Allianz Green Transition Tracker 2026:
1. India's GHG emissions fell 0.2% in 2025 despite about 7.6% economic growth.
2. Globally, renewables overtook coal in electricity generation.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Both: India's emissions fell 0.2% to 4,508 MtCO2e; renewables 33.5% vs coal 33.2%.

s: According to the World Bank's International Debt Report 2026, the external debt of developing countries in 2025 reached a record
x: It rose 5.5% to a record $9.4 trillion in 2025.

s: As per the International Debt Report 2026, India's external debt in 2025 stood at about
x: India: $763.5 bn in 2025 vs $717.4 bn in 2024 (about 6.4% growth).

s: In the International Debt Report 2026, external debt grew fastest (8.1% to $1.3 trillion) among countries eligible for concessional financing from
x: IDA-eligible countries' debt rose 8.1% to $1.3 trillion.

s: Which is India's highest-ranked institution in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027?
x: IIT Delhi at 66th (59th last year); IISc 79th, IIT Bombay 83rd, IIT Madras 85th.

s:
Consider the following about QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027:
1. No Indian university is in the top 50.
2. India's number of ranked institutions rose to 325.
3. QS is headquartered in the USA.
Which of the above are correct?
x: No Indian institution in the top 50 for the 2nd year; India 325 (from 294); QS is UK-based.

s: Which university secured the first position in Andhra Pradesh in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027?
x: SRM University-AP, Amaravati, was first in AP and among the top 100 in Southern Asia.

s: Which city was ranked India's cleanest city overall in Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 (awards on 11 Nov 2026)?
x: Navi Mumbai 1st, Surat 2nd, Vijayawada 3rd; Indore moved to the mentor-city role.

s: In Swachh Survekshan 2025-26, which city was ranked cleanest among cities with more than 10 lakh population?
x: GVMC Visakhapatnam was 1st, Jabalpur 2nd, Lucknow 3rd.

s: Under the new 'Swachh Shehar Jodi' (mentor–mentee) category of Swachh Survekshan 2025-26, which pair from Andhra Pradesh was ranked 3rd?
x: Ranks: Ahmedabad–Sanand, Indore–Depalpur, Tirupati–Kuppam.

s:
Consider the following about Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 awards:
1. They were conferred by President Droupadi Murmu at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
2. The survey is conducted by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Swachh Survekshan is by MoHUA; Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan (air) is by MoEFCC.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh city was ranked 3rd in the 3–10 lakh population category of Swachh Survekshan 2025-26?
x: Ujjain 1st, Chandigarh 2nd, Guntur 3rd.

s: Which of the following was NOT among Andhra Pradesh's six award-winning ULBs in Swachh Survekshan 2025-26?
x: The six: Greater Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Guntur, Tirupati, Rajamahendravaram and Kuppam.

s: Which State ranked first in the Access (In)Equality Index (AEI) 2026, in which Andhra Pradesh was second?
x: Goa 1st (0.68), AP 2nd (0.66), Sikkim 3rd.

s:
Consider the following about the Access (In)Equality Index 2026:
1. It is prepared by the Centre for New Economic Studies, O.P. Jindal Global University.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranked first in the socio-economic security dimension.
3. It assesses three dimensions with 60 indicators.
Which of the above are correct?
x: CNES (Jindal) prepares it; AP led socio-economic security (0.69); it has five dimensions, not three.

s: Which State topped the Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index (EVOI) released in November 2026?
x: AP 1st, Kerala 2nd, Tamil Nadu 3rd, Delhi 4th; UP last.

s: The Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index was prepared by
x: It is by startup body IndiaTech.org with consumer organisation Consumer VOICE.

s: In Andhra Pradesh's Public Health Services Performance Assessment (October 2026), which district ranked first in patient satisfaction?
x: Palnadu 81.6%, Polavaram 81.5%, Nellore 80.7%; Kurnool last (69.5%).

s: The report 'The Participation Paradox: Women's Work and Time-Use in India' (2026) was released by
x: ICRIER released it using PLFS and Time Use Survey data.

s:
As per ICRIER's 'The Participation Paradox' (2017-18 to 2025):
1. The number of working women nearly doubled from 104 million to 201 million.
2. The female Worker Population Ratio rose from 22% to 38%.
3. A rural woman now earns about 53% of a rural man's earnings, up from 45%.
Which of the above are correct?
x: Statement 3 is reversed: the ratio fell from 53% to about 45%.

s: According to the India Employment Report 2024 (ILO–IHD), roughly what share of India's workforce is informally employed?
x: Nearly 90% of the workforce is informal even as unemployment fell from 6.1% to 3.2%.

s: Who won the Booker Prize 2026?
x: M. John Harrison won for 'The End of Everything'.

s: The novel that won the Booker Prize 2026 is
x: 'The End of Everything' by M. John Harrison; 'Flesh' won in 2025.

s:
Consider the following about the Booker Prize 2026 winner:
1. At 81, he is the oldest winner of the prize.
2. The winning novel is a science-fiction work.
3. The jury was chaired by Mary Beard.
Which of the above are correct?
x: All correct: Harrison (81) is the oldest winner, from the SF world; chair Mary Beard.

s: The prize money of the Booker Prize (for the winner) is
x: £50,000, plus £2,500 to each of the six shortlisted authors.

s: Match the prize with its 2026 winner: International Booker Prize 2026
o: The End of Everything – M. John Harrison
x: International Booker 2026 went to Taiwan Travelogue (tr. Lin King); Heart Lamp won in 2025.

s: From 2027, the International Booker Prize will be renamed as the
x: It becomes the Bukhman International Booker Prize (£100,000) from 2027.

s: Nirmala Lakshman's 'The Tamils: A Portrait of a Community' won the Best International Non-Fiction Book award at
x: It won at the Sharjah International Book Fair Awards, presented by Sheikha Bodour bint Sultan Al Qasimi.

s: Dr Devi Shetty was honoured by France in November 2026 with the
o: Chevalier de l'Ordre national du Mérite
Ordre des Arts et des Lettres
x: He received the Chevalier de l'Ordre national du Mérite for Covid-era support to the French community.

s:
Consider the following about France's Ordre national du Mérite:
1. It was founded by Charles de Gaulle in 1963.
2. It is France's highest national order.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Founded 3 Dec 1963 by de Gaulle; it is the second-highest, after the Legion of Honour (founded by Napoleon, 1802).

s: The Indian NGO REACH received the Kochon Prize 2026 for its work against
x: The Kochon Prize (Kochon Foundation, Korea, with the Stop TB Partnership) honours work against TB.

s:
Consider the following about the Kochon Prize 2026:
1. REACH is the first Indian civil-society non-profit to receive it.
2. It is awarded by WHO's Global TB Programme.
3. It was shared with organisations from Kenya and the Marshall Islands.
Which of the above are correct?
x: It is given by the Kochon Foundation with the Stop TB Partnership, not WHO.

s: 'StopBleed', which won a top honour at Singapore's Slingshot 2026, is
o: An AI app for blood-bank logistics
A nano-biopolymer haemostatic powder that controls severe bleeding in about 60 seconds
x: It is a haemostatic powder by Sabir Hussain's Miracules Medsolutions, approved by CDSCO as a Class C device.

s: Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu was recognised in November 2026 among the '38 by 38' Achievers of
x: Purdue's College of Engineering award (instituted 2024), inspired by alumnus Neil Armstrong.

s:
Assertion (A): Purdue University's award for young alumni is called '38 by 38'.
Reason (R): Purdue alumnus Neil Armstrong walked on the Moon at the age of 38.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: The award honours 38 alumni under 38 and is inspired by Armstrong's Moon walk at 38.

s: Which of the following manuscripts were added to UNESCO's Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register in November 2026?
o: Bhagavad Gita, Tirukkural and Gita Govinda
x: Mahabharata (Vyasa), Rajatarangini (Kalhana) and Arthashastra (Kautilya) were added in 2026.

s: Match the work with its author: Rajatarangini
x: Rajatarangini is by Kalhana; Arthashastra by Kautilya; Panchatantra by Vishnu Sharma.

s: The Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union (ABU), which honoured Prasar Bharati in 2026, is headquartered at
x: ABU (est. 1964) is headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

s: Which Akashvani station's programme 'Beyond the Call' won the Audio PSA Special Commendation at the ABU Prizes 2026?
x: Prasar Bharati–Akashvani, Bengaluru, for 'Beyond the Call'.

s: A ₹250 commemorative coin was released in November 2026 to mark the 250th birth anniversary of
x: FM Nirmala Sitharaman released it for Muthuswami Dikshitar (1775–1835).

s: Muthuswami Dikshitar used which mudra (signature) in his compositions?
x: Dikshitar's mudra was Guruguha; Syama Sastri's was Syama Krishna.

s: The 'Best Mechanical Engineering Student Award 2026' won by J.T. Amareswar of Vijayawada was conferred by
x: The Indian Society for Technical Education (ISTE), AP Section, on 7 Nov 2026.

s: Sanjit 'Bunker' Roy, who died in November 2026, founded the Barefoot College at
x: He set up the SWRC at Tilonia, Rajasthan, in 1972 – later the Barefoot College.

s:
Consider the following honours received by Bunker Roy:
1. Padma Shri (1986)
2. Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement (2004)
3. Ramon Magsaysay Award (2010)
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Padma Shri 1986 and Tyler Prize 2004 are correct; in 2010 he was in the TIME 100 list, not a Magsaysay award.

s: Prof. Ashok Kumar Mahapatra, who died in November 2026, was the founding Director of
x: He was founding Director of AIIMS Bhubaneswar and received the Padma Shri in 2025.
